title: Holiday lights and inflatables: safe teardown
summary: Get LEDs and mini bulbs, thin twin wire, plug fuses, low-voltage adapters, inflatable blower fans and fabric, solar panels with their rechargeable cells, and coin cells out of holiday decorations. Light strings and some inflatables run on mains, and the coin cells in tea lights can kill a child who swallows one.

steps.text: Unplug every light string, inflatable and adapter at the wall, then unplug the strings from each other. Keep the plugs where you can see them. Switch off anything with batteries. Let anything that was lit cool completely before you touch its lamps (Gemmy AB-2-E manual). Lights still up on eaves or trees: unplug them at the outlet, then take them down from a non-metal ladder with a helper holding it, keeping three points of contact and passing things down rather than carrying them.
steps.warn: A string joined to one still plugged in is live. Always unplug at the wall first.

steps.text: Work where children can't reach and keep a jar with a lid on the bench for coin cells. Sort what you have: keep working sets whole (see the notes), and never bridge their plug fuse or fit a bigger one. A set with cut, frayed or bare wire, cracked lamp holders or loose connections is for parts only: never plug it back in. GE says to discard such a set (GE 50 mini set sheet), and CPSC says to throw out damaged sets (CPSC holiday decorating).

Tea lights and small light-up pieces: undo the battery door (the Sterno candles have a screw, then a coin turn) and take out the coin cell, a CR2032 in the Sterno (Sterno candle sheet). Put each cell into its own small bag, or tape over it, then into the lidded glass or plastic jar, so no cell touches another or any metal (NWRA lithium storage).
steps.warn: A swallowed coin cell can cause severe internal burns within about two hours (CPSC Reese's Law). If a child may have swallowed one, get them to emergency care at once.

steps.text: Battery figures: open the battery box and take out the cells. The SVI 12 ft skeleton takes four C cells, and its box is under the pelvis (SVI skeleton sheet). Don't climb to it: SVI says the 12 ft figure must be laid down for disassembly, with three adults advised (SVI skeleton sheet). Bag any cell with white crust or leaks.
steps.warn: Leaked alkaline crust burns skin and eyes. Wear gloves and wash your hands after.

steps.text: Solar strings: switch the light off, undo the screw on the battery cover under the solar panel and take out the cell, one 1.2 V AA NiMH in the Glitzhome set (Glitzhome solar string sheet). Do this before you cut any wire.
steps.warn: The panel charges the cell by day (Glitzhome solar string sheet), so keep the cell's ends off metal and out of children's reach.

steps.text: Mains light strings you are stripping: cut the plug off, leaving a short tail. Then slide open the fuse cover on top of the plug with a small screwdriver and take out the fuses (3 A, 125 V in the GE sets: GE 50 mini set sheet, GE 50 LED set sheet).
Pull each bulb or LED with its plastic base straight out of its holder (GE 50 LED set sheet). Don't twist. Bag them by type and write the rating from the set's tag on the bag.
steps.warn: Mini bulbs are thin glass. Wear safety glasses and don't squeeze them.

steps.text: Cut the wire between the holders and coil it, or cut the holders off and keep the long runs. Tie each coil and label it as light-string wire.
steps.warn: Use this thin wire only on low-voltage DC. Never use it in anything that plugs into the wall. Some PVC wire coatings contain lead: wash your hands before you eat (OEHHA holiday lights).

steps.text: Inflatables with an adapter (Gemmy 13-E-DTC): unplug the adapter from the fan's lead. Find the fan by its air intake, free it from the fabric (undo its fixings, or cut the fabric round its mount), and cut its lead well away from the fan. Keep the adapter whole and its label readable (Gemmy 13-E-DTC manual).

Inflatables that plug straight into the wall (Gemmy AB-2-E, 120 V with a fuse in its plug and 7 W C7 lamps): cut the plug off first, then open the zipper and take out the lamps (glass: wear safety glasses) and their holders, and the fan (Gemmy AB-2-E manual). Mark the fan as a mains part.
steps.warn: Gemmy rates the whole product 120 V, so treat its fan as mains-powered until its own label says otherwise (Gemmy AB-2-E manual).

steps.text: Cut the inflatable's fabric into the biggest flat panels you can, along the seams, with a knife or scissors. Keep any zippers.

Light projectors: read the label. If it shows a laser warning or a laser class, keep the laser in its housing, don't power it on, and never look into its window. Never point it at the sky or an aircraft: the FAA warns holiday laser displays can briefly blind or distract pilots, and says aiming one at an aircraft breaks federal law (Nextgov FAA laser displays; see the laser card).
steps.warn: Laser light can injure eyes, even from a reflection. Never point a laser at people, animals, vehicles or aircraft (see the laser card).

steps.text: Test what you kept (see the notes) and label it OK or BAD.

notes:
## Before you strip it

Working light sets are worth keeping whole where you have mains, a generator or an inverter. They use little power: a GE 50-light incandescent mini set is rated 20.4 W (GE 50 mini set sheet) and a GE 50-light LED set 12 W (GE 50 LED set sheet). Outdoors, use only sets marked for outdoor use, plugged into a GFCI (RCD) outlet, and never exceed the total wattage on the tag when joining sets (GE 50 LED set sheet). Don't put mains lights on a metal tree, and switch them off when you sleep (CPSC holiday decorating). A blown plug fuse means an overload or a short: unplug the set and anything joined to it, fit a fuse of the same rating only, never bridge it or fit a bigger one, and discard the set if the new fuse blows too (GE 50 mini set sheet, Gemmy AB-2-E manual).

## What's worth keeping and why

- **LEDs.** The GE LED sets use 3.3 V, 0.066 W lamps (GE 50 LED set sheet), which is about 20 mA each. On low-voltage DC, put a resistor in series: ohms = (supply volts − 3.3) ÷ 0.02. About 100 Ω for one LED on 5 V USB, about 470 Ω on 12 V. Good for night lights, indicators and torch repairs.
- **Mini bulbs.** The GE incandescent set uses 2.5 V, 0.425 W bulbs (GE 50 mini set sheet), about 0.17 A each. Two NiMH cells (2.4 V) light one: a pilot lamp or a battery tester.
- **Plug fuses.** 3 A, 125 V in the GE sets (GE 50 mini set sheet) and 5 A, 125 V in the Gemmy AB-2-E (Gemmy AB-2-E manual). Spares for small low-voltage circuits, at the same rating: never fit a bigger fuse in place of a smaller one.
- **Wire.** Long runs of thin twin wire for low-voltage DC: LED lighting, sensors, alarm wiring (see build_perimeter_alarm), tying and lashing. Some PVC coatings contain lead, so wash your hands after handling it and keep it from children's mouths (OEHHA holiday lights).
- **Adapters.** The Gemmy 13-E-DTC adapter gives 12 V, 1.5 A (Gemmy 13-E-DTC manual) and the SVI skeleton's 5.9 V, 1.5 A (SVI skeleton sheet). Read each label: volts, amps and the polarity symbol. Use only on gear needing the same voltage and no more current.
- **Inflatable fans.** A ready blower. If an adapter-fed fan's adapter (Gemmy 13-E-DTC) is marked 12 V DC, the fan probably runs on 12 V, but the manual prints no rating for the fan itself: read its label, match the polarity, and test it first on a bench supply set to 12 V with the current limited to the adapter's 1.5 A. The Gemmy AB-2-E is rated 120 V as a whole (Gemmy AB-2-E manual), so treat its fan as a mains part. A steady draught for a small forge, a rocket stove or drying food: keep the plastic fan well back from heat.
- **Fabric.** Light fabric for covers, bags and patches. Gemmy says rips can be sewn by hand or taped with clear packing tape (Gemmy 13-E-DTC manual). Test how well it sheds water before you rely on it.
- **Solar panel, cell and light sensor.** The Glitzhome solar string charges one AA NiMH cell by day and switches on by itself in the dark (Glitzhome solar string sheet): a ready solar night light (see teardown_solar_garden_light).
- **Coin cells.** CR2032, 3 V (Sterno candle sheet), for watches, scales, remotes and small sensors. Keep them away from children, each in its own small bag or taped over, in a lidded glass or plastic jar so none touch each other or metal (NWRA lithium storage).

## Testing what you got out

- **Adapters.** Plug in and measure the output: within about 5% of the label is good.
- **LEDs.** Meter on diode test makes one glow faintly, or use a coin cell or a resistor as above.
- **Fans.** Adapter-fed fans: feed the adapter's label voltage from a bench supply (30 V or less), fingers clear. Mains fans: only through an RCD (GFCI), terminals covered, with hands and loose clothing clear of the blades.
- **Solar panel.** In full sun, measure its open-circuit volts (see test_solar_panel).
- **Coin and NiMH cells.** A fresh CR2032 reads about 3 V; a charged NiMH cell about 1.3–1.4 V.

## Variations

- **Mains incandescent mini sets, GE model CFPD(I)-50(0.17).** 50 bulbs, 2.5 V, 0.425 W each; 20.4 W; indoor only; 3 A fuses in the plug (GE 50 mini set sheet).
- **Mains LED sets, GE model C3LED(I)-5.5MMa-50(0.1).** 3.3 V, 0.066 W LEDs with no shunts, so the set may not light if one LED fails; 12 W; join sets only up to 24 W in all (GE 50 LED set sheet).
- **Adapter inflatables (Gemmy 13-E-DTC).** A DTC adapter, model MTR-18W120S150-UL, 12 V, 1.5 A; a fan that keeps it up; LEDs that can't be replaced (Gemmy 13-E-DTC manual).
- **Mains inflatables (Gemmy AB-2-E).** 120 V, 60 Hz; a polarized plug with a 5 A fuse; 7 W C7 candelabra lamps behind a zipper; the fan motor may stop below −10 °C (14 °F) (Gemmy AB-2-E manual).
- **Big figures (SVI 12 ft skeleton).** Four C cells or a 5.9 V, 1.5 A adapter; LCD eyes (SVI skeleton sheet).
- **Solar strings (Glitzhome).** One 1.2 V AA 600 mAh NiMH cell under the panel (Glitzhome solar string sheet).
- **Flameless tea lights (Sterno).** One CR2032 behind a screwed door (Sterno candle sheet).
- **Laser light displays.** The FAA has warned owners not to aim holiday laser displays at the sky because they can briefly blind or distract pilots, and that deliberately aiming one at an aircraft breaks federal law (Nextgov FAA laser displays).

## If a child swallows a coin cell

Go to emergency care at once (CPSC Reese's Law). On the way, CPSC passes on the National Capital Poison Center's advice: a child over 12 months who swallowed one within the last 12 hours can be given 10 mL of honey every 10 minutes, up to six doses. Don't delay the trip to get honey (CPSC Reese's Law).

## What to leave

- Plug-in adapters and controller boxes: keep them closed.
- Broken bulbs, and sets with scorched or melted plastic.
- Leaking batteries: bag them, labelled.
- Laser modules from light projectors: leave them in their housings.
